subject: Confirming fiscal delegate and kickoff contacts
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@medlytics.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Confirming fiscal delegate and kickoff contacts

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: You mentioned the pilot use case (clinical notes summarization) and a preference for a predictable per-transaction cost with enterprise-grade audit logs.
- Ask: Can you confirm who will be the signing/fiscal delegate for this purchase and who we should loop in from procurement and security for an initial sync? That will help us tailor the SOW and prepare the required security artifacts.
- Ask 2: Any procurement timing constraints (quarterly PO cycles, legal blackout dates) we should be aware of?

What would be most helpful: the name and preferred email for the economic buyer, the procurement lead (who handles vendor onboarding), and the security contact for SOC2/data handling questions. If you prefer, share a short roster and we'll send a one-pager + SOW template ahead of the procurement call.

I'm copying Ben (solutions) and Marissa (AE) so we can coordinate the next meeting. We can be flexible, but if it helps to lock something, we have 30–45 minute windows Wed/Thu next week (your timezone).

Attachments: will send a one-pager and SOW template once you confirm the right recipients.

Thanks — look forward to the next step.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com]

Rachel —

Thanks for the follow-up and the clear recap. Per our internal notes: 

- Economic buyer / fiscal delegate: Tom Walters, CFO — tom.walters@medlytics.io (he signs larger pilots and platform contracts).
- Procurement lead (vendor onboarding and PO): Elena Park, Head of Procurement — elena.park@medlytics.io.
- Security contact for evaluation and evidence requests: Will Chan, Senior Infosec Engineer — will.chan@medlytics.io.

Procurement timing: we close procurement reviews on a two-week cadence; Elena has a vendor review slot the week of Mar 13. Tom is out of town Mar 6–9 but available for a short call in the afternoons Mar 8 or Mar 14.

Next step preferred by our team: a 30–45 minute procurement & security sync with Elena + Will + Tom present if possible. Can you share your one-pager and an SOW/MSA template before that meeting? Also we typically route initial contracts through our central legal — happy to include their contact after the sync.

Samantha
Director, Product 
MedLytics

Tom / Elena / Will — great to meet you (virtually). Per Samantha's note, our recommended next step is a 30–45 minute procurement + security alignment so we can: 

1) Walk through the pilot scope, expected call volumes, and success criteria (so we can lock an accurate cost estimate).
2) Surface the security artifacts you typically request (SOC2 Type II, access controls, data handling/retention).
3) Share a draft SOW and MSA template so procurement/legal can flag any non-starters early.

Suggested slots (Pacific time): 
- Wed Mar 8, 11:00–11:45 PT
- Thu Mar 9, 09:30–10:15 PT
- Tue Mar 14, 13:00–13:45 PT

I've attached the Redwood one-pager and a sample SOW to this thread for your review. If none of those slots work, please propose alternatives.

Quick internal note before we lock the procurement call: 

- Can we prepare a short pricing band (pilot estimate) and an "estimated TCO ribbon" for Tom — he usually wants a 12-month view showing peak vs. average consumption.
- Include the standard performance SLA bullets (p50/p90 latency, uptime, support response) in the SOW attachment so procurement sees them up front.
- Ben — can you draft a two-slide summary for the procurement meeting that highlights integration points and data handling? I can own the contract language highlights.

If we share the one-pager + TCO estimate ahead of the call, it will make the Elena review slot far more productive.

Marissa

Redwood Inference
